request.message: What is the thickness range of the Shale Grit in the southern part of the Sheet?

response.answer: The Shale Grit is 450 to 550 feet thick in the southern part of the Sheet. [E1]

evidences.doc_title: The Geology of the Country Around Holmfirth and Glossop (excerpt)
evidences.text:
GENERAL STRATIGRAPHY
The Shale Grit forms a wide spread on the moors in the
southern part of the Sheet, where it is 450 to 550 feet'thick.It is
also cxposed in the valleys of the Etherow and Tame. In the
south it consists of grits and sandstones with frcquent thin sandy
shale beds and less frequent thicker shale beds; in Longdendale
the exposed part of the series consists of thicker and more massivc
grits, but theexposures in the Tame valley show the beds to be more
like those in the south.
